html:
SMTO-LLM-0101 — The selected model can't read images

GUID: 51c2e422-b9ea-5df2-a2c6-c9f43c8f0480
Slug: attachment-vision-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: vision

What happened

  • SMTO needs a model whose service confirms it accepts pictures, but the model chosen for image work hasn't confirmed that. The image wasn't sent to it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and find the Vision card. If it says Use Main, your Main model is being used for images. This shows which model SMTO tried to use for your picture.
  2. On the Vision card, enter an Endpoint and Model that support images, then select Save Vision. SMTO only sends pictures to a model whose service reports that it accepts images; the model's name alone isn't enough.
  3. Start a new task and ask about the image again. Tasks keep the model settings they started with, so only new tasks use the saved Vision model.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's reply describes what is in the image instead of showing this error.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who runs the model service to confirm the model is served with image support turned on (some models need an extra image file loaded with them), and send them the details from Copy error details. Until this works, don't rely on any SMTO answer about that image; it wasn't looked at.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The active Vision route's serving metadata does not advertise image input for the current endpoint and model, so the image request was refused before it was sent.

What this means

  • Active serving metadata does not explicitly advertise image input for the current endpoint/model identity. A model name is not capability evidence. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Active serving metadata does not explicitly advertise image input for the current endpoint/model identity. A model name is not capability evidence.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Configure the Vision role with an endpoint whose model metadata reports image_input=true (for llama.cpp or vLLM, serve the model with its matching multimodal projector), or rely on Main as fallback only if it advertises image input. Model names are not treated as capability evidence; start a new task to pick up the change.
  • Configure an image-capable Vision connection for a new task. Verify the serving model and its matching projector; use Main as fallback only when it advertises image input.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual serving endpoint advertises image input and a bounded visual request returns a meaningful observation.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
